question: How do I submit a grievance?
answer: You can submit a grievance directly here in the chat — just say 'submit a grievance' or 'I have a complaint' and I will walk you through it. Alternatively, you can use the 'New Grievance' form on the portal homepage. You'll need your name, GBU email/roll number, the grievance category, and a short description.

question: What information do I need to file a grievance?
answer: You need your full name, GBU registered email or roll number, the department/category the issue relates to (Academic, Hostel, Examination, Fee, Infrastructure, or IT), and a clear description of the issue. Supporting documents can be attached on the portal form if needed.

question: What is a Ticket ID and where do I get it?
answer: A Ticket ID is a unique reference code (format: GBU-YYYY-NNNNN) generated automatically the moment your grievance is submitted. It is shown on screen immediately and also emailed to your registered address. Keep it safe — you'll need it to track your grievance status.

question: How can I track the status of my grievance?
answer: Enter your Ticket ID here in the chat (e.g., GBU-2026-00123) or use the 'Track Grievance' option on the portal. I'll show you the current status: Pending, In Progress, or Resolved, along with the last updated date.

question: What do the grievance statuses mean?
answer: Pending means your grievance has been received but not yet assigned. In Progress means a department officer is actively working on it. Resolved means action has been taken and a resolution note has been added; you'll also receive an email confirming closure.

question: How long does it take to resolve a grievance?
answer: Most grievances are acknowledged within 24-48 hours and resolved within 7 working days, depending on complexity. Academic and examination-related grievances may take slightly longer due to committee review. You'll be notified by email at every stage.

question: Will I get notified about updates to my grievance?
answer: Yes. The system sends a mandatory email notification when your grievance is submitted and again whenever its status changes, so you always know where things stand without needing to check manually.

question: What categories of grievances can I file?
answer: You can file grievances under six categories: Academic (courses, faculty, grades), Examination (results, revaluation), Hostel (accommodation, mess, maintenance), Fee (payments, refunds, dues), Infrastructure (labs, classrooms, campus facilities), and IT/Portal (login issues, website bugs).

question: What if my grievance is not resolved on time?
answer: If your grievance stays Pending beyond the expected timeline, you can request an escalation here in the chat, or contact the IT Cell / Grievance Redressal Committee directly. Escalated tickets are flagged for priority review by senior administration.

question: Can I edit or withdraw a grievance after submitting it?
answer: Once submitted, the core details of a grievance cannot be edited to preserve record integrity, but you can add follow-up comments using your Ticket ID. To withdraw a grievance, mention your Ticket ID here and request withdrawal — this will be logged and reviewed by an admin.

question: Is my grievance confidential?
answer: Yes. Grievance details are only visible to you and authorized admin staff handling your case. Your identity is not shared publicly, and sensitive complaints (e.g., harassment) are routed to a restricted-access queue.

question: Do I need to log in to submit a grievance?
answer: Yes, you need to log in with your GBU student credentials so the system can verify your identity and link the grievance to your academic record for accurate follow-up. This also prevents spam submissions.

question: Who do I contact for urgent issues?
answer: For urgent or safety-related issues, please contact the IT Cell / Grievance Redressal Committee directly through the official university helpdesk rather than waiting for the standard grievance workflow, since this chatbot handles routine queries and status tracking.

question: The portal is not loading or showing an error, what do I do?
answer: Try clearing your browser cache or switching browsers first. If the issue persists, you can report it here as an 'IT/Portal' category grievance and our team will investigate. Include a screenshot on the web form if possible.

question: I was charged incorrectly, how do I raise a fee grievance?
answer: File a grievance under the 'Fee' category with your transaction ID, amount, and date of payment. The finance office typically reviews fee-related grievances within 5 working days and refunds are processed after verification.

question: Can I file a grievance anonymously?
answer: Standard grievances require you to be logged in for accountability and follow-up, but sensitive complaints such as harassment or ragging can be filed with restricted visibility so only the designated committee sees your identity, not the general admin queue. Ask the assistant to route your complaint as 'sensitive' if you need this.

question: Can I file more than one grievance at a time?
answer: Yes, there's no limit on the number of open grievances you can have. Each one gets its own unique Ticket ID and is tracked independently, so unrelated issues should always be filed as separate grievances rather than combined into one.

question: Can I attach documents or screenshots to my grievance?
answer: Yes, on the full grievance form (portal homepage) you can attach supporting documents such as fee receipts, screenshots, or medical certificates up to 10 MB per file. The chat-based quick submission currently supports text only — for evidence-heavy complaints, use the portal form instead.

question: I lost my Ticket ID, how do I find it?
answer: Check the confirmation email sent to your registered GBU email address at the time of submission — the Ticket ID is included there. If you can't locate the email, contact the IT Cell helpdesk with your name and roll number and they can look it up for you.

question: Can I check the status of someone else's grievance?
answer: No. For privacy reasons, grievance status can only be checked using the Ticket ID together with your logged-in account matching the original submitter. If you're a parent or guardian following up, the student should share updates directly or authorize the IT Cell to disclose them.

question: What counts as a working day for resolution timelines?
answer: Working days are Monday through Saturday, excluding declared university holidays and Sundays. A grievance filed on a Friday evening, for example, is typically acknowledged by the following Monday, and the 7-working-day resolution clock starts once it's officially assigned.

question: Do all grievance categories have the same resolution timeline?
answer: No. Fee grievances are typically resolved within 5 working days, Hostel and Infrastructure issues within 3-7 days depending on whether physical inspection is needed, IT/Portal bugs within 2-4 days, while Academic and Examination grievances can take 10-15 days since they often require committee or faculty review.

question: I'm not receiving email notifications, what should I do?
answer: First check your spam/junk folder, since university-domain emails are sometimes filtered. Confirm the email address on your grievance matches your active inbox. If notifications still don't arrive after 24 hours, report it as an 'IT/Portal' grievance so the team can check the mail delivery logs.

question: How do I raise a grievance about unfair grading?
answer: File a grievance under the 'Academic' category, mentioning the course code, faculty name, and the specific assessment you're disputing. Grading disputes are reviewed by the Academic Grievance Sub-Committee, which may request the answer script or assignment for evaluation before a decision.

question: Can I complain about a faculty member's conduct?
answer: Yes, conduct-related complaints against faculty are filed under 'Academic' and are automatically treated as sensitive, meaning they're routed to a restricted queue visible only to the Dean of Academic Affairs and the Grievance Redressal Committee chair, not general department staff.

question: What if my attendance shortage was due to a genuine reason?
answer: File an 'Academic' grievance explaining the reason (medical, family emergency, official university representation, etc.) along with supporting documents attached via the portal form. Condonation requests are reviewed by the department's academic committee, typically within 10 working days.

question: How do I request revaluation of my exam paper?
answer: File a grievance under 'Examination', mentioning the subject code, exam date, and roll number. Revaluation requests must typically be raised within 7 days of result declaration and carry a nominal fee handled separately through the Fee category if a change in marks is not granted.

question: My exam result hasn't been declared yet, what do I do?
answer: Result delays are usually posted as announcements on the university portal first. If your result is missing well past the announced date while others in your batch have theirs, file an 'Examination' grievance with your roll number and subject codes so the Examination Cell can investigate.

question: I missed my exam due to a medical emergency, what are my options?
answer: File an 'Examination' grievance immediately, ideally within 3 days of the missed exam, and attach medical proof via the portal form. The Examination Committee decides whether you're eligible for a special/supplementary exam on a case-by-case basis.

question: How do I complain about hostel room allotment?
answer: File a 'Hostel' category grievance mentioning your current room number, hostel block, and the specific issue (overcrowding, maintenance, roommate conflict, etc.). Room reallotment requests are reviewed by the Chief Warden and typically processed within a week, subject to availability.

question: How do I report a mess food quality issue?
answer: File a 'Hostel' grievance describing the specific issue (hygiene, quality, menu deviation, timing) with the date it occurred. Recurring mess complaints are also reviewed collectively at the monthly Mess Committee meeting, so repeated reports on the same issue help build the case.

question: Who do I contact about hostel maintenance issues like broken furniture or plumbing?
answer: File a 'Hostel' grievance with your room/block number and a description of the maintenance issue. These are routed directly to the hostel maintenance team and are usually the fastest category to resolve, often within 2-3 working days for straightforward repairs.

question: How do I report a problem with campus WiFi or internet?
answer: File an 'Infrastructure' or 'IT/Portal' grievance mentioning the specific building/block and the nature of the issue (no connectivity, slow speed, frequent disconnects). The Network team typically resolves connectivity issues within 2-3 working days.

question: How do I complain about classroom or lab equipment?
answer: File an 'Infrastructure' grievance specifying the room number, building, and equipment concerned (projector, AC, lab instruments, seating, etc.). These are routed to campus facilities management and prioritized based on whether the issue is actively disrupting classes.

question: How do I report a safety hazard on campus?
answer: Safety hazards (broken flooring, exposed wiring, poor lighting in walkways, etc.) should be filed as 'Infrastructure' grievances marked urgent, and are escalated immediately to campus security and facilities. For anything posing immediate danger, also contact campus security directly rather than waiting for the grievance workflow.

question: I can't log in to the grievance portal, what should I do?
answer: First try resetting your password using the 'Forgot Password' link with your registered GBU email. If that doesn't work, it may be an account sync issue between the university ERP and the grievance portal — in that case, message the assistant here with your roll number so we can log it as an IT/Portal issue for the tech team.

question: How do I report a bug or glitch I found on the university website?
answer: File an 'IT/Portal' grievance describing the exact page/URL, what you did, and what went wrong (a screenshot helps a lot — attach it via the portal form). The IT Cell development team reviews and prioritizes bugs based on how many users are affected.

question: How do I formally escalate a grievance to higher authorities?
answer: Mention your Ticket ID here and say you'd like to escalate — this flags it for review by the Grievance Redressal Committee chair rather than the department officer originally assigned. Escalation is intended for cases that are significantly overdue or where you're unsatisfied with the resolution offered, not as a first step.

question: I'm not satisfied with how my grievance was resolved, can I appeal?
answer: Yes. Reply with your Ticket ID and mention you'd like to appeal the resolution within 7 days of the ticket being marked Resolved. The Grievance Redressal Committee will review the original decision and may reopen the case if new information is presented.

question: How long is my grievance data stored?
answer: Grievance records, including your submitted details and correspondence, are retained for the duration of your enrollment at GBU plus 3 years for audit and compliance purposes, after which they are archived or securely deleted as per university data retention policy.

question: Who has access to my grievance details?
answer: Only the department officer assigned to your case and the Grievance Redressal Committee (for escalations) can view your grievance details. Sensitive categories such as harassment complaints are further restricted to a small designated panel, and access is logged for accountability.

question: How do I report harassment or ragging?
answer: Harassment and ragging complaints can be filed here under the appropriate category and are automatically flagged as sensitive, routing them directly to the Anti-Ragging Committee or Internal Complaints Committee rather than the general grievance queue. For anything involving immediate safety risk, also contact campus security or the university helpline directly rather than waiting on the grievance workflow.

question: I'm a new student and don't have portal credentials yet, how do I file a grievance?
answer: New students receive their GBU login credentials during orientation/registration. If you haven't received yours yet, you can still describe your issue here in the chat and the assistant will guide you to the IT Cell to get provisional access so your grievance can be formally logged against your record.

question: Can faculty or staff also file grievances through this system?
answer: This chatbot and portal are primarily configured for student grievances. Faculty and staff grievances are handled through a separate HR/Establishment grievance channel — if you're staff, please contact the HR department directly rather than filing here.

question: Can alumni or former students file a grievance?
answer: Alumni can file grievances related to matters that arose during their enrollment (e.g., degree certificate errors, transcript issues) but should use their alumni-registered email since student portal credentials are deactivated after graduation. Mention 'alumni' in your description so it's routed correctly.

question: How do I request a fee refund after withdrawing from a course?
answer: File a 'Fee' category grievance mentioning the course/program withdrawn from, the amount paid, and your transaction reference. Refunds are processed as per the university's refund policy schedule, which varies depending on how many days before the semester start you withdrew.

question: My scholarship or fee waiver wasn't applied correctly, what do I do?
answer: File a 'Fee' grievance with your scholarship reference number/order and the discrepancy in the amount charged. These are reviewed jointly by the Finance Office and the Scholarship Cell, typically within 7-10 working days since it may require cross-checking with the scholarship provider.

question: What are the IT Cell's working hours?
answer: The IT Cell helpdesk is available Monday to Saturday, 9:30 AM to 5:30 PM, excluding university holidays. Grievances can be filed through this chatbot and the portal 24/7 — they'll simply be picked up for processing on the next working day if submitted outside these hours.

question: Is support available in Hindi as well as English?
answer: This chatbot currently responds in English, but you're welcome to describe your issue in Hindi or a mix of both and the assistant will do its best to understand it. For formal grievance records, however, please provide the final description in English so it's clearly understood by the reviewing department.

question: What can this chatbot actually do?
answer: I can help you submit a new grievance, track an existing one by Ticket ID, answer questions about the grievance process using the official knowledge base, and guide you on escalation or appeal steps. For anything requiring a human decision — like actually resolving your case — it's handled by the relevant department officer, not by me.

question: Are your answers always accurate?
answer: I answer policy and process questions using a retrieval-augmented system grounded in the official GBU grievance knowledge base, so I won't invent rules that don't exist. That said, for legally binding or highly specific edge cases, I'll point you to the IT Cell or Grievance Redressal Committee to confirm directly.

question: Can I give feedback on how my grievance was handled?
answer: Yes, once your ticket is marked Resolved, the confirmation email includes a short feedback link where you can rate the resolution and add comments. This feedback is reviewed periodically by the Grievance Redressal Committee to improve response quality across departments.

question: Can I use the grievance system from my phone?
answer: Yes, both the chat assistant and the grievance portal are mobile-responsive and work in any modern mobile browser — there's no separate app required. You can submit, track, and receive email notifications about your grievance entirely from your phone.

question: Where is Gautam Buddha University located?
answer: Gautam Buddha University is located on the Yamuna Expressway in Greater Noida, Gautam Buddha Nagar district, Uttar Pradesh (PIN 201312), part of the Delhi National Capital Region. The campus spans about 511 acres.

question: When was Gautam Buddha University established?
answer: GBU was established by the Uttar Pradesh Gautam Buddha University Act (No. 9) of 2002 and started its first academic session in August 2008. It's a state government university funded jointly by NOIDA and Greater Noida Industrial Development Authority (GNIDA), and is UGC-recognized with NAAC B+ accreditation.

question: What is Gautam Buddha University / what does GBU stand for?
answer: GBU stands for Gautam Buddha University, a state government university in Greater Noida, Uttar Pradesh, offering undergraduate, postgraduate, and doctoral programs across engineering, management, computer applications, biotechnology, law, humanities, and Buddhist studies, with a strong research focus.

question: How do I contact the university directly (not the grievance system)?
answer: You can reach GBU's main office at +91-120-2344200 or info@gbu.ac.in, or visit the official website at www.gbu.ac.in for department-specific contacts, admissions, and general information not related to grievances.
